$comment: The concern registry of §6.1 (G-P6) — versioned data inside @plat/kernel (C-0005), append-only: each row keeps the u16 id it was appended with; ids are never renumbered or reused; a new concern is a reviewed change appended at the end (C-0020). Rows in §6.1's table order, one per concern; `row` is the table row it shares; `cap` the attempt cap as the table writes it ("default" or a number; null for a retired id); `keyedBy` the table cell verbatim, the one statement of how its draws are keyed; `readers` the reader stages or programs the cell names; `reservedUntil` the milestone whose item lands the first reader (no field: read at M0). ConcernId constants are generated from this file into ids.ts (test/rng/gen-registry.ts). Item M0-d-01.

rows.name: plan.damage
rows.keyedBy: geometry-free; non-rerollable by salt; epoch component 0. Item 123's damage thresholds (§6.3 *Plan damage*): one uniform per plan element, keyed by (the building's lineage, the element's id) at the stage id its `plan.*` concerns carry, no rung counter, reroll or salt entering — fixed for the element's life, never re-drawn; read by every reader that draws a plan's damage: §2.6 step 7's damage layer, V03 (the plan's drawing per state, its exports, the panel lines), V02 (the exterior), V04 (cellars, crypts and underground buildings), §8.6 and §11.1

rows.name: view.weather
rows.keyedBy: view only; non-rerollable. The weather timeline (item 124; *The weather stream*, below): keyed from the session seed by the spell index, never from the seed key; the spell's marks (§8.2's *Weather effects*: positions, lengths and sways) on further keys of the same concern — the spell's entity key folded through the one mixer with the frame's world-aligned cell as structured components — so a mark stays put while its spell lasts; read by §8.4's per-frame weather layer and §8.2's effect marks, which §8.8 places above the tiles — never by a stage, a digest, a tile key or an export
